system:
You read drug labels and paper abstracts for a biotech investment analysis and extract evidence for the
translation chain of one mechanism. For every document list each finding:
- drug: one of the given drug names, or TARGET when the finding is about the target itself (knockout, knockdown,
  model organism) rather than a drug. Each document says which drug it is about (about_drug): a result in that
  document that names no drug ("in the 100 mg group") is about that drug.
- link: animal_response (effect in an animal or cell model of the disease), exposure (the drug reaches the site of
  action: plasma, tissue or CSF levels, half-life), target_engagement (the drug binds, blocks or lowers its target, for
  example receptor occupancy or lower target protein or mRNA), pd_response (a downstream biomarker changes),
  clinical_benefit (a clinical endpoint in patients).
- result: shown or not_shown. not_shown only when the text says it was looked for and not found or not met.
- species: human, animal or cell.
- in_disease: true if the finding is in the given disease.
- quote: copied word for word from the document, at most 30 words, that states the finding.
Rules: a finding is a RESULT the document reports from a study (a measurement, a comparison with placebo or
baseline, an observed change, an endpoint met or missed). General statements about what a drug does, is designed to
do or "plays a role in" are not findings. Use only what the document says; do not use outside knowledge; do not count
planned or ongoing studies as results; skip findings about other drugs. Return every document id you were given, with an empty list if nothing.
user: {"disease": "amyotrophic lateral sclerosis", "target": "SOD1", "drugs": ["DRUGOMERSEN", "OTHERSEN"], "documents": [{"id": "doc:01", "about_drug": "DRUGOMERSEN", "text": "In the Phase 1 part, drugomersen reduced total SOD1 protein in cerebrospinal fluid by 35% compared with placebo in adults with ALS."}, {"id": "doc:02", "about_drug": "DRUGOMERSEN", "text": "Drugomersen concentrations in CSF increased with dose and were measurable in all participants."}, {"id": "doc:03", "about_drug": "DRUGOMERSEN", "text": "Plasma neurofilament light chain, a marker of axonal injury, fell by 50% with drugomersen and rose with placebo."}, {"id": "doc:04", "about_drug": "DRUGOMERSEN", "text": "PET imaging showed 70% receptor occupancy in the motor cortex four hours after a single dose of drugomersen."}, {"id": "doc:05", "about_drug": "DRUGOMERSEN", "text": "Drugomersen met its primary endpoint: ALSFRS-R decline was slower than with placebo (difference 3.1 points, P=0.01)."}, {"id": "doc:06", "about_drug": "OTHERSEN", "text": "After intravenous dosing, othersen was not detected in cerebrospinal fluid in any participant."}]}

findings.quote: drugomersen reduced total SOD1 protein in cerebrospinal fluid by 35% compared with placebo in adults with ALS.
Drugomersen concentrations in CSF increased with dose and were measurable in all participants.
Plasma neurofilament light chain, a marker of axonal injury, fell by 50% with drugomersen and rose with placebo.
PET imaging showed 70% receptor occupancy in the motor cortex four hours after a single dose of drugomersen.
Drugomersen met its primary endpoint: ALSFRS-R decline was slower than with placebo (difference 3.1 points, P=0.01).
After intravenous dosing, othersen was not detected in cerebrospinal fluid in any participant.
